verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 33% to $1.39B as product revenue posted its strongest sequential dollar growth ever — but $402M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $326M and a net loss of $296M.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers paying to store and analyze data on Snowflake's platform, billed mostly by how much they use. Up 34% YoY.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Consulting and training that help customers get started. Up 25% YoY.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 28% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 13% YoY.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Down 39% YoY from $210M.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $123.42 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — and other income covered only $2.12 of the gap, leaving a $21.25 loss per $100. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: Other income of $29M, net: $41M of interest income, less $2M of interest expense and $10M of other expense, net.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $1,390,951K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $166M (a 12% margin) and adjusted free cash flow was $266M, a 19.1% margin. Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $326M; other income and a small tax benefit covered part of that, so the chart draws the remaining $296M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source.

takeaways.title: Product growth hit an inflection point
takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 34% to $1,334M — the strongest sequential dollar growth in Snowflake's history — and management raised full-year product revenue guidance to $5,840M, up 31%.

takeaways.title: Stock pay is the loss, on paper
takeaways.text: Stock-based compensation was $402M in the quarter — larger than the entire $296M net loss. It is a real cost to shareholders through dilution, but it is not cash out the door: adjusted free cash flow was $266M.

takeaways.title: Customers keep expanding
takeaways.text: Net revenue retention was 126% — existing customers spent 26% more than a year ago — and 779 customers now spend over $1M a year on the platform, up 29%. Remaining performance obligations rose 38% to $9.21B.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation of $402M (cash-flow statement figure) sits inside every cost line and is the main reason GAAP results show a loss while non-GAAP results show a profit.
General and administrative costs fell 39% YoY to $129M — the year-ago quarter's $210M was unusually heavy, which flatters the comparison.
